title: Usage Insights API: Route detail endpoint (model breakdown + deltas + caching)
creator: Chloe Martin
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
description:
Goal
Build the Route Detail API endpoint that powers the console route detail page. The endpoint must return:
- Summary metrics for a route in a given time window
- Model breakdown for that route (top models by cost) including cost + performance metrics
- Deltas vs prior period (“what changed”) for key metrics
- A caching strategy that keeps p95 low for interactive use while preserving correctness and RBAC boundaries

Context
This is part of the “In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)” initiative. Console needs a detail view when a user clicks a route from the Top Routes list. That view shows spend + latency/error trends and answers: “which models are driving spend on this route” and “what changed vs last week / prior period”.

References
- Confluence API contract addendum: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-analytics-api-contract.json
- ADR route definition/normalization: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-route-dimension-definition-and-normalization.json
- Aggregates dataset work: ENG-8422
- Route list endpoint: ENG-8423

Scope
1) Endpoint
- Add GET route detail endpoint under the insights service.
- Proposed shape (aligning with contract):
  - GET /v1/analytics/usage-insights/routes/{route}/detail
  - Query params: start_ts, end_ts, environment, region, project_id (optional if derived from auth), deployment_mode (optional), model_limit (default 10), include_unknown_model (default true)
- Response includes:
  - route (canonical)
  - window: start_ts/end_ts and computed “prior_window” start/end
  - summary:
    - total_cost_usd
    - input_tokens, output_tokens
    - cached_input_tokens, cached_output_tokens (if available in aggregates)
    - unit_cost_usd_per_1k_tokens (derived)
    - p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms
    - error_rate (5xx + upstream inference errors as defined by Caleb’s spec)
    - request_count
  - deltas_vs_prior:
    - absolute and percent change for: total_cost_usd, request_count, p95_latency_ms, error_rate, input_tokens, output_tokens
    - note: percent_change is null when prior is 0 (avoid divide-by-zero); console handles display
  - model_breakdown: array of top models by total_cost_usd, each with same metric set as summary (scoped to route+model)
  - “other_models_rollup” bucket when model_limit truncates (to keep UI consistent and prevent long tables)

2) Delta definition (“prior period”)
- prior_window is the immediately preceding window of equal duration: [start_ts - (end_ts-start_ts), start_ts)
- Deltas computed on the server so console doesn’t need to coordinate multiple calls.
- For “All time” or very long ranges, enforce max window length (see guardrails) to keep query costs bounded.

3) Data source and query strategy
- Use hourly aggregates when requested window <= 72h; otherwise daily aggregates.
- Late-arriving events: aggregates are eventually consistent; we do not attempt to stitch raw events here.
- All queries must be scoped by org_id + (project_id or project set from auth context) + environment.

4) Caching strategy
Primary goal: keep p95 < 250ms for typical “last 7 days” route detail view under dashboard load while controlling DB cost.

- Layer 1: application in-memory cache (per instance)
  - TTL: 30s
  - Key: org_id|project_id|route|start_ts|end_ts|env|region|deployment_mode|model_limit
  - Notes: best-effort; safe to drop. Use for bursty console refresh.

- Layer 2: shared Redis cache (authoritative for this endpoint)
  - TTL: 120s default; 30s for windows <= 1h (faster-moving), 300s for windows >= 7d
  - Key must include org_id and project_id to avoid cross-tenant leaks.
  - Store: full serialized response + a “generated_at” timestamp.
  - Do not cache error responses except for 404 route-not-found (TTL 60s) to dampen repeated bad requests.

- Cache invalidation
  - Time-based TTL only for MVP.
  - No write-through invalidation triggered by late aggregates (we’ll rely on freshness SLO + TTL).

- HTTP caching
  - Do not set public cache headers.
  - Add ETag based on response hash to allow console to revalidate; still scoped to authenticated context.

5) Guardrails
- Enforce maximum time range: 31 days for this endpoint (return 400 with actionable message).
- Enforce model_limit between 1 and 25.
- Enforce route length/character constraints consistent with ADR normalization rules.
- If route is missing from aggregates, return 404 with: code=ROUTE_NOT_FOUND and include a hint about “Unknown route” + route tagging docs.

6) RBAC / tenancy
- Endpoint must respect org/project boundaries. Use the same scoping middleware as ENG-8423.
- If user has org access but not project access, return 403.
- Security review required specifically for caching key composition and ensuring we never cache responses without org+project in key.

Acceptance criteria
- Endpoint implemented and documented in internal API contract notes.
- Returns correct summary + model breakdown for a known route.
- Returns deltas vs prior window for key metrics and handles prior=0 safely.
- Uses hourly vs daily rollups based on window length.
- Implements Redis caching with TTLs as defined above; includes org_id+project_id in cache key.
- Meets performance budgets in staging load test:
  - p95 <= 250ms for last 7d window, model_limit=10, warm cache
  - p95 <= 800ms cold cache with DB query (baseline; can adjust after measurements)
- Unit tests:
  - prior window computation
  - percent delta semantics
  - cache key composition includes tenant identifiers
  - 400 validation for max window + model_limit
- Integration tests:
  - RBAC scoping (cannot query another project’s route)
  - truncation behavior (other_models_rollup)

Implementation notes
- Prefer a single query per aggregate table per window (current + prior) and compute deltas server-side.
- Consider precomputing route+model totals in a CTE and selecting top N models by cost.
- Ensure query uses partition predicates (date/hour) to avoid full scans.

Observability
- Emit metrics:
  - usage_insights.route_detail.request_count
  - usage_insights.route_detail.db_query_ms
  - usage_insights.route_detail.cache.hit (labels: layer=in_memory|redis)
  - usage_insights.route_detail.response_bytes
  - usage_insights.route_detail.errors (labels: code)
- Add tracing spans around: auth scope resolution, cache lookup, DB query, response serialization.

Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag: usage_insights_route_detail_api
- Enable in staging for dogfood, then beta orgs.
- Monitor: cache hit rate, p95, DB query time, 4xx/5xx rates.

Linked work / deliverable
- Implementation PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-15462.json

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should prior window align to calendar boundaries (week-over-week)?
  - A: No for MVP; we use preceding equal-duration window for consistent deltas.
- Q: Should route be identified by route_id vs canonical string?
  - A: Use canonical route string in path; server normalizes and uses normalized_route for lookup; reject if normalization changes semantics (return 400 with normalized suggestion).
comments: 2026-01-21 (Paula Mendes): Please make sure “what changed” covers both spend and latency; the UI will highlight p95 delta and total cost delta. We should avoid requiring console to issue a second call for prior window.

2026-01-23 (Allison Grant): Cache key MUST include tenant scope; I’ve seen leaks from missing project_id in other services. Also ensure we can measure cache hit rates per layer and alert on DB query time regressions.

2026-01-27 (Thomas Baird): Route normalization should happen before cache key generation, otherwise we’ll create multiple cache entries for equivalent routes. Also enforce route length cap early to avoid unbounded keys.

2026-02-03 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): RBAC: ensure auth middleware resolves project scope from token when project_id omitted. If project_id is provided, confirm it’s within the caller’s allowed set; otherwise 403.

2026-02-10 (Caleb Johnson): For error_rate, use the shared definition from latency/error telemetry: numerator = (gateway_5xx + inference_error) / request_count. Don’t include 4xx (bad prompts) in error rate for SLO views.

2026-02-14 (Jada Williams): Implemented endpoint + caching + delta computation in PR-15462. Added other_models_rollup bucket and tightened max window validation to 31d. Load test on staging shows warm-cache p95 ~180ms for 7d window; cold-cache p95 ~640ms.

2026-02-18 (Marcus Lin): Security review: OK with Redis caching provided key includes org_id + project_id + normalized_route, and cached payload never includes any cross-project fields. Please ensure ETag is computed post-authorization (not shared across tenants).
